sehemu: Part II: Public Leaders' Ethics Secretariat
maudhui: (1) There shall be a Public Leaders' Ethics Secretariat which shall have authority to investigate the conduct and behaviour of any public leader for the purpose of ensuring that the provisions of the Public Leadership Code of Ethics law are properly observed. (2) For purposes of this Article, the meaning of a public leader and the requirements of public leadership ethics shall be understood in accordance with the Public Leadership Code of Ethics law or any other law enacted by Parliament insofar as those provisions concern leadership and its definition. (3) The Ethics Secretariat shall consist of an Ethics Commissioner and such other employees as may be prescribed by a law enacted by Parliament. (4) Parliament shall enact a law prescribing principles of public leadership ethics to be observed by all persons holding offices specified by a law enacted by Parliament. (5) The principles of public leadership ethics shall: (a) define the offices to which they apply; (b) require persons holding specified offices periodically to make formal declarations concerning their income, assets and liabilities; (c) prohibit conduct which tends to show dishonesty, favouritism or lack of integrity, tends to promote or encourage corruption in public affairs, or jeopardizes the interests or welfare of society; (d) prescribe penalties for breach of the principles; (e) prescribe procedures, powers and practices for ensuring compliance; and (f) make any other appropriate and necessary provision for promoting and maintaining honesty, transparency, impartiality and integrity in public affairs and protecting public funds and other public property. (6) Parliament may by law provide for the dismissal or removal from office of a person for breach of leadership ethics, whether the office is elective or appointive.
